meta.description: Browse Reddit better on your mobile than ever before!
meta.title: Acorn × Reddit for mobile

body: Acorn is an open source Reddit client. You can read every line of code on <github>GitHub</github>.
Acorn has no servers, accounts or databases of its own. We don't show ads, we don't use analytics or tracking, and we don't sell or share your data with anyone.
sections.title: Overview

body: You sign in on Reddit's own login page. Acorn never sees or stores your password.

After you sign in, Acorn keeps the session that Reddit issues so it can load your feed and act on your behalf. Everything you do in the app, like browsing, voting, posting, commenting, messaging and uploading media, goes directly from your device to Reddit and is covered by Reddit's <reddit>privacy policy</reddit>.
sections.title: Your Reddit account

body: Your signed in accounts, preferences and gestures are stored on your device and synced between your devices through your iCloud account. Your read history, collapsed comments, sort orders and filters are stored only on your device. We have no access to any of this.
iCloud sync is provided by Apple and covered by Apple's <apple>privacy policy</apple>.
sections.title: Data on your device

body: When something goes wrong, Acorn sends an error report to Sentry so we can fix it. Reports include the error, technical details about your device and app version, and your Reddit username. A very small sample of performance data is also collected. Refer to Sentry's <sentry>privacy policy</sentry>.
sections.title: Crash reporting

body: Some media, like RedGIFs videos and GIPHY images, is loaded directly from the service that hosts it. Like any website, these services can see your IP address when your device connects to them.
Subscriptions are processed by Apple. We never see your payment details; the app only checks with the App Store whether you have an active subscription.
Translation uses Apple's built in translation feature.
App updates are delivered through Expo, whose servers receive standard request information when the app checks for updates. Refer to Expo's <expo>privacy policy</expo>.
sections.title: Other services

body: Acorn only asks for access to your photo library when you choose to save media or attach media to a post. It isn't used for anything else.
sections.title: Permissions

body: This website doesn't use cookies, analytics or collect any data.
sections.title: Website

body: Acorn isn't meant for children under 13, or the minimum age required by Reddit in your country.
sections.title: Children

body: You can remove an account by signing out, and remove all local data by deleting the app. If you'd like crash reports linked to your username deleted, reach out to us.
sections.title: Your choices

body: If this policy changes, we'll update it here along with the date at the top. Questions? Reach out on <discord>Discord</discord> or <github>GitHub</github>.
sections.title: Changes and contact

body: By downloading or using Acorn, you agree to these terms. If you don't agree, please don't use the app.
sections.title: Agreement

body: Acorn is an independent, third party app. It isn't affiliated with, endorsed, sponsored or approved by Reddit, Inc. Reddit is a trademark of Reddit, Inc.
sections.title: Not affiliated with Reddit

body: When you use Reddit through Acorn, you're still using Reddit. You're responsible for following Reddit's <redditTerms>User Agreement</redditTerms>, content policy and community rules, and Reddit's <reddit>privacy policy</reddit> applies to everything you do there.

Reddit controls how third party apps can access its platform, including through its <redditApi>Data API Terms</redditApi>. Reddit doesn't officially approve every way third party apps connect to it, and may consider using an unofficial app a violation of its terms.
sections.title: Reddit's terms still apply

body: Reddit can change, limit or shut off access for third party apps at any time, without notice. If that happens, some or all of Acorn may stop working, and we can't promise we'll be able to fix it.

Reddit may also restrict, suspend or ban accounts it believes are using unauthorized apps or tools. By using Acorn, you accept this risk, and we aren't responsible for any action Reddit takes against your account.
sections.title: Use at your own risk

body: Acorn doesn't host any content. Posts, comments, media and everything else you see belong to their authors and are provided by Reddit and other services. We aren't responsible for that content.
sections.title: Content

body: Don't use Acorn to break the law, spam, harass others, scrape data, or get around Reddit's rules or limits.
sections.title: Acceptable use

body: Subscriptions are sold and billed by Apple through the App Store and are governed by Apple's <appleEula>terms</appleEula>. You can manage or cancel them in your App Store settings, and refunds are handled by Apple. A subscription supports Acorn's development; it doesn't guarantee that Reddit will keep allowing access.
Except where required by law, payments are non-refundable, including when features stop working or Acorn stops working entirely because of changes made by Reddit or another third party.

We may, at our sole discretion, help with a refund or offer another remedy in some cases, for example if we choose to discontinue Acorn for reasons within our control. Any such remedy is a courtesy decided case by case, and doesn't create an obligation to offer the same or any remedy in other situations.
sections.title: Subscriptions

body: We may change, suspend or discontinue Acorn, or any part of it, at any time. If Reddit ends access in a way we can't work around, we'll stop selling new subscriptions and let existing subscribers know as soon as we reasonably can, so they can cancel renewals.
sections.title: Changes to the app

body: Acorn's source code is available under the <license>GNU GPL v3</license>. These terms cover the app we distribute, not your rights under that license.
sections.title: Open source

body: Acorn is provided "as is" and "as available", without warranties of any kind. We don't guarantee the app will be available, accurate, secure or free of bugs.
sections.title: No warranty

body: To the fullest extent allowed by law, we aren't liable for any indirect, incidental or consequential damages, or for any loss of data, content or account access, that results from using or being unable to use Acorn.
To the same extent, our total liability for any claim relating to Acorn is limited to the amount you paid for Acorn in the 12 months before the claim.
Some places don't allow certain warranties or liabilities to be excluded or limited. If you live in one of them, these terms don't take away any consumer rights you have under the law there.
sections.title: Limitation of liability

body: Our <privacy>privacy policy</privacy> explains what data Acorn handles.
